newsitem.title: USA: Denver asks high court to review key munibond case.
newsitem.headline: Denver asks high court to review key munibond case.

text.p: Denver asked the U.S. Supreme Court to review a recent federal appeals court ruling that said private investors can sue municipalities for damages under the anti-fraud provisions of the federal securities laws.

Attorneys for the city and county of Denver said in a brief filed with the high court on Wednesday that the November 1996 ruling by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit is wrong and "raises serious public policy concerns."
The 10th Circuit had refused to throw out a set of challenges brought by Bonnie Sonnenfeld and other investors in Denver International Airport bonds.
The investors charged that the city had made inadequate disclosures to investors about costly construction delays for the $5 billion facility.
Denver said in yesterday's brief that the appeals court decision is "unprecedented" and violates Congress' intent that private rights of action be granted sparingly.

"Given the increasing importance of the state and local government securities market, the 10th Circuit's decision has significance far beyond the parties to this case," lawyers for Denver said in the petition, City and County of Denver, Colorado, vs Bonnie Sonnenfeld (96-1268).
